cia_pra_a:
| Address | Chip | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0xBFE001 | CIAA | pra | Peripheral Data Register A |

Reads the current state of Port A pins. Each bit reflects the combined state of the output latch (where DDRA=1) and the actual pin level (where DDRA=0).

| Bit | Pin | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | /FIR1 | Fire button 1 input (joystick port 2) — active low |
| 6 | /FIR0 | Fire button 0 input (joystick port 1) — active low |
| 5 | /RDY | Disk ready — active low (0 = disk is ready) |
| 4 | /TK0 | Track 0 — active low (0 = head is over track 0) |
| 3 | /WPRO | Write protect — active low (0 = disk is write-protected) |
| 2 | /CHNG | Disk change — active low (0 = disk was removed/inserted) |
| 1 | /LED | Power LED — 0 = LED on (output, DDRA bit 1 = 1) |
| 0 | OVL | Overlay Kickstart ROM — 1 = ROM mapped at $000000 on startup (output, DDRA bit 0 = 1) |

DDRA typical value: **0x03** (bits 0-1 are outputs: OVL and /LED; bits 2-7 are inputs from floppy/joystick).
cia_prb_a:
| Address | Chip | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0xBFE101 | CIAA | prb | Peripheral Data Register B (Parallel Port) |

Connects to the Amiga's parallel port (DB25 connector). All 8 bits map to parallel port data pins D0-D7.

| Bit | Function |
| --- | --- |
| 7-0 | Parallel port data bits D7-D0 |

DDRB determines input (0) vs output (1) for each bit. Timer A/B can optionally appear on PB6/PB7 via CRA/CRB PBON and OUTMODE bits.
cia_pra_b:
| Address | Chip | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0xBFD000 | CIAB | pra | Peripheral Data Register A (Serial/Parallel Control) |

Controls RS-232 serial port handshake lines and Centronics parallel port status.

| Bit | Pin | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | /DTR | Data Terminal Ready — serial port output |
| 6 | /RTS | Request To Send — serial port output |
| 5 | /CD | Carrier Detect — serial port input |
| 4 | /CTS | Clear To Send — serial port input |
| 3 | /DSR | Data Set Ready — serial port input |
| 2 | SEL | Parallel port SELECT — input |
| 1 | POUT | Parallel port PAPER OUT — input |
| 0 | BUSY | Parallel port BUSY — input |

DDRA typical value: **0xFF** (all outputs, drives all lines from software).
cia_prb_b:
| Address | Chip | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0xBFD100 | CIAB | prb | Peripheral Data Register B (Floppy Drive Control) |

Directly controls floppy disk drive motor, selection, and head step signals.

| Bit | Pin | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | /MTR | Motor control — 0 = motor on (all selected drives) |
| 6 | /SEL3 | Drive 3 select — 0 = DF3: selected |
| 5 | /SEL2 | Drive 2 select — 0 = DF2: selected |
| 4 | /SEL1 | Drive 1 select — 0 = DF1: selected |
| 3 | /SEL0 | Drive 0 select — 0 = DF0: selected |
| 2 | /SIDE | Side select — 0 = upper head, 1 = lower head |
| 1 | DIR | Step direction — 0 = step inward (higher track), 1 = step outward |
| 0 | /STEP | Step pulse — pulse low to move head one track |

DDRB typical value: **0xFF** (all outputs).
cia_ddr:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| DDRA | Data Direction Register A — controls pin direction for Port A |
| DDRB | Data Direction Register B — controls pin direction for Port B |

For each bit position: **1 = output**, **0 = input**.

When a bit is an output, writing to the corresponding PRx register bit drives that pin. When a bit is an input, reading PRx returns the actual pin state.

| Chip | Register | Typical Value | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CIAA | DDRA | 0x03 | Bits 0 (/LED) and 1 (OVL) are outputs; bits 2-7 are floppy/fire inputs |
| CIAA | DDRB | 0x00 | Parallel port defaults to all inputs |
| CIAB | DDRA | 0xFF | All serial/parallel control lines are driven by CIA |
| CIAB | DDRB | 0xFF | All floppy drive control lines are outputs |
cia_timer:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| TALO / TAHI | Timer A low and high byte — 16-bit countdown timer |
| TBLO / TBHI | Timer B low and high byte — 16-bit countdown timer |

Each CIA contains two independent 16-bit interval timers (A and B). Each timer has:
- A **counter** register that counts down from the latch value to 0
- A **latch** register that holds the reload value

On **read**: returns the current counter value (actively decrementing).
On **write**: stores the value into the latch (does not affect running counter unless LOAD is strobed via CRA/CRB bit 4).

Timer clock source: **0.715909 MHz** (NTSC) or **0.709379 MHz** (PAL) — derived from the E-clock (CPU clock / 10).

| Mode (CRA/CRB bit 3) | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| RUNMODE = 0 | Continuous — reloads from latch and continues counting after underflow |
| RUNMODE = 1 | One-shot — stops after first underflow, clears START bit |

An underflow triggers the corresponding interrupt source (Timer A or Timer B) in the ICR.

Timer A period = (latch value + 1) / timer_clock_hz

> Example: latch = 0x0708 (1800 decimal), PAL: period ≈ 2.538 ms ≈ 394 Hz
cia_tod:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| TODLO | Time of Day counter bits 7-0 |
| TODMID | Time of Day counter bits 15-8 |
| TODHI | Time of Day counter bits 23-16 |

The TOD (Time of Day) is a 24-bit binary counter that increments on every vertical blank (CIAA) or horizontal sync (CIAB) signal.

| Chip | Clock Source | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CIAA | VSync (50 Hz PAL / 60 Hz NTSC) | Counts seconds/minutes/hours in BCD or raw 50/60Hz ticks |
| CIAB | HSync | Counts scanlines (approx. 15,625 Hz PAL / 15,734 Hz NTSC) |

**Reading**: Reading TODHI latches all three TOD registers so they can be read consistently (prevents tearing between bytes). The latch is released after TODLO is read.

**Writing**: Writing TODHI stops the TOD counter until TODLO is written (allows atomic 3-byte update).

**Alarm**: An alarm value can be set via the TOD registers while CRB bit 7 (ALARM) is set to 1. When the TOD counter reaches the alarm value, a TOD interrupt fires (ICR bit 2 = TOD).
cia_sdr:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| SDR | Serial Data Register — 8-bit bidirectional shift register |

The Serial Data Register (SDR) implements a byte-serial interface using the CNT (count/clock) and SP (serial port data) pins.

| Mode (CRA bit 6 = SPMODE) | Function |
| --- | --- |
| 0 = Input | Data is shifted in on SP pin, clocked by falling edge of CNT. When 8 bits are received, an SP interrupt fires (ICR bit 3). |
| 1 = Output | Writing to SDR loads the shift register. Data is shifted out on SP pin, clocked by the internal timer A (which must be running in continuous mode). When transmission is complete, an SP interrupt fires. |

**CIAA usage**: The Amiga keyboard controller sends key data to CIAA.SDR via the SP pin, clocked by CNT. Each key event produces an 8-bit keycode (7 bits + direction bit). The keyboard handshake line (/KBRESET) is driven by the MCU.

**CIAB usage**: Not used in standard Amiga configurations.
cia_icr:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ICR | Interrupt Control Register — dual-function (read = data, write = mask) |

The ICR operates as two overlapping registers at the same address:

**Read (DATA register)** — returns current interrupt state:

| Bit | Name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | IR | Master interrupt flag — 1 if any enabled interrupt is pending |
| 6 | — | Reserved, reads 0 |
| 5 | FLG | FLAG pin interrupt — triggered by /FLAG pin going low |
| 4 | S_P | Serial Port interrupt — SDR byte sent/received |
| 3 | TOD | Time of Day alarm interrupt |
| 2 | B | Timer B underflow interrupt |
| 1 | A | Timer A underflow interrupt |
| 0 | — | Reserved, reads 0 |

Reading the ICR clears all interrupt flags (bits 0-5) and deasserts the interrupt line.

**Write (MASK register)** — enables or disables interrupt sources:

| Bit | Name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | SET/CLR | 1 = set the mask bits written as 1; 0 = clear the mask bits written as 1 |
| 5-1 | FLG/S_P/TOD/B/A | Enable/disable corresponding interrupt source |

> Note: CIAA interrupt output → CPU **INT2** (level 2). CIAB interrupt output → CPU **INT6** (level 6).
cia_cra:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CRA | Control Register A — configures Timer A and the serial port |

| Address | Chip |
| --- | --- |
| 0xBFEE01 | CIAA |
| 0xBFDE00 | CIAB |

| Bit | Name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | — | Unused, always reads 0 |
| 6 | SPMODE | Serial port mode: **1** = output (CNT sources shift clock); **0** = input (external clock required) |
| 5 | INMODE | Timer A input: **1** = counts positive CNT transitions; **0** = counts E-clock (Ø2) pulses |
| 4 | LOAD | Force load (strobe): **1** = immediately reload counter from latch. Reads back as 0; writing 0 has no effect |
| 3 | RUNMODE | **1** = one-shot (auto-stops after underflow); **0** = continuous (reloads and continues) |
| 2 | OUTMODE | Timer A output on PB6: **1** = toggle on underflow; **0** = pulse on underflow |
| 1 | PBON | **1** = Timer A output appears on PB6; **0** = PB6 is normal I/O |
| 0 | START | **1** = start Timer A; **0** = stop Timer A. Auto-clears on underflow in one-shot mode |
cia_crb:
| Register | Description |
| --- | --- |
| CRB | Control Register B — configures Timer B and the TOD alarm |

| Address | Chip |
| --- | --- |
| 0xBFEF01 | CIAA |
| 0xBFDF00 | CIAB |

| Bit | Name | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 7 | ALARM | TOD alarm: **1** = writes to TOD registers set the alarm; **0** = writes update the TOD counter |
| 6 | INMODE1 | Timer B input mode bit 1 (combined with INMODE0): see table below |
| 5 | INMODE0 | Timer B input mode bit 0: see table below |
| 4 | LOAD | Force load (strobe): **1** = immediately reload counter from latch. Reads back as 0 |
| 3 | RUNMODE | **1** = one-shot; **0** = continuous |
| 2 | OUTMODE | Timer B output on PB7: **1** = toggle; **0** = pulse |
| 1 | PBON | **1** = Timer B output appears on PB7; **0** = PB7 is normal I/O |
| 0 | START | **1** = start Timer B; **0** = stop Timer B |

**INMODE1:INMODE0 — Timer B input source:**

| INMODE1 | INMODE0 | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | E-clock (Ø2) pulses — same as Timer A default |
| 0 | 1 | Positive CNT pin transitions |
| 1 | 0 | Timer A underflow pulses |
| 1 | 1 | Timer A underflow while CNT pin is held high |
